Subject: Re: Acme RFP: Security architecture questionnaire

Hi Jared — thanks for sending. We've completed our initial pass on the questionnaire and attached a concise packet with the architecture diagram and threat summary. Highlights below; see attachments for full answers and references.

Highlights (summary):
- Isolation model: logical tenant isolation in hosted mode via per-tenant request namespaces, strict routing layers, and per-tenant KV cache keys. For Dedicated/Private deployments we offer VPC-isolated clusters and options to pin workloads to dedicated GPU pools.
- Network model: control plane (managed by Redwood) is segmented from data plane (model inference nodes). Control plane uses mutual TLS and private peering; data plane endpoints can be placed in customer VPCs for Private deployments. Diagram: network-diagram-v1.png attached.
- Data protection: customer-provided plaintext is only kept in-memory during inference; not written to persistent storage in hosted mode. All at-rest storage (model weights, temp caches) uses AES-256 GCM. KMS integration (customer or cloud KMS) for key wrapping.
- Logging and telemetry: request traces and token-level cost metadata are stored with PII redaction by default. Audit logs (access, admin actions) are retained per plan and can be exported to customer S3/GCS destinations.
- Threat model: we summarize primary attacker classes (external tenant access, supply-chain, insider, network MITM) and mitigations (RBAC, guardrails, signed model artifacts, kernel-level hardening). See threat-model-summary.docx.

Attachments: redwood-security-arch-answers.pdf, network-diagram-v1.png, threat-model-summary.docx

We can schedule a technical deep-dive next week to walk their security team through the diagram and hit any follow-ups. Proposed: May 18 at 10:00am PT.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme RFP: Security architecture questionnaire — internal review notes

Rohan — great first draft. I reviewed the packet and propose a few clarifications before we send the final to Acme's team: 

1) Data residency and persistence: emphasize that in Hosted mode we do not persist customer prompt/response pairs to disk except for short-term prefix caching (TTL configurable). Model weights are managed separately and never contain customer data.
2) Audit log redaction: default behavior is to redact token-level content; we should specify retention tiers (30 days default, configurable up to 1y for enterprise).
3) Private deployment flow: add explicit sequence when customer requests VPC peering — control plane endpoints use mTLS with cert pinning and ephemeral credentials; add a callout on KMS enforcement for private key material.
4) Threat model: add a short section on LLM-specific data leakage vectors (prompt leakage via KV cache) and our mitigation (cache scoping + automatic scrubbers on metadata exports).

I've attached an annotated version of the network diagram with callouts: network-diagram-annotated.png. Please incorporate these notes into the PDF answers and update the threat-model-summary.docx. Also cc Laura if we need an exec note on retention policy for enterprise pricing.

- Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Rohan / Mina — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Our security reviewers had two clarifying questions after looking at the diagram and the threat summary: 

1) Logging retention and PII: Can you confirm the default retention window for request-level logs in Hosted mode and whether PII is redacted by default? What's the process to export logs to our S3 with customer-side encryption?

2) Third-party dependencies: do you run any third-party model optimization or tracing agents in production that could access raw requests (e.g., telemetry from runtime vendors)? If so, what controls are in place (SCAs, signed binaries, limited access)?

I've attached a short follow-ups workbook: Acme_RFP_followups.xlsx.

We still hope to have your final packet by May 20; can you confirm availability for a May 18 technical review as previously suggested?

Regards,
Jared
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Acme RFP: Security architecture questionnaire — answers and next steps

Hi Jared — answers inline and updated artifacts attached. Thanks for the pointed questions.

1) Logging retention & PII: Default request-trace retention in Hosted is 30 days. Token-level content is redacted by default; request metadata and cost telemetry are retained. For enterprise customers we offer configurable retention tiers (30/90/365 days) and automatic export to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket with SSE (server-side encryption) or customer-managed keys via KMS. The export process uses signed transfer endpoints and can be configured to use customer-prescribed encryption. See section 3.2 of redwood-security-arch-answers.pdf.

2) Third-party dependencies: We do not run external telemetry agents that capture raw request payloads in production. We maintain a small set of vetted runtime libraries from well-known vendors; all binaries are signed and verified during our build pipeline. Any third-party service that requires access to logs or metrics must go through an approval workflow; we record these approvals in audit logs. See third-party section in threat-model-summary.docx.

Changes made: updated redwood-security-arch-answers.pdf to reflect Mina's edits, added network-diagram-annotated.png, and appended a one-page threat model executive summary. All attachments are in the Drive link below.

Proposed next steps: confirm May 18 10:00am PT for the technical review and we'll prepare a short walk-through deck focusing on the network flow and tenant isolation. Please let us know any additional follow-ups by EOD 2026-05-17.

Attachments: redwood-security-arch-answers.pdf, network-diagram-annotated.png, threat-model-summary.docx

Best regards,
Rohan Mehta
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
